findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses bare `pub status: String` and independent `pub is_validated: bool` / `pub is_sent: bool` fields, making illegal states fully constructible (e.g. status="sent" with is_sent=false, or status="" with is_sent=true). No typestate or enum enforces the lifecycle.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct or mutate LedgerWorkflow into an inconsistent lifecycle state; validation and sending flags diverge from the nominal status string with no invariant enforcement.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a domain enum (e.g. `LedgerStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent }`) and fold `is_validated`/`is_sent` into the enum or a typestate wrapper so the compiler rejects invalid combinations.

findings.problem: `pub is_validated: bool` is a primitive boolean lifecycle flag. Per the functional-core-performance reference, bool lifecycle flags must be replaced with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: A bool provides no domain meaning at the type level; callers cannot pattern-match on validation state, and the compiler cannot enforce that validation is a prerequisite for sending.
findings.fix: Replace with an enum variant inside the status type (e.g. `LedgerStatus::Validated`) or a dedicated `ValidationState` enum.

findings.problem: `pub is_sent: bool` is a primitive boolean lifecycle flag. Per the functional-core-performance reference, bool lifecycle flags must be replaced with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: No type-level guarantee that `sent_at_epoch_ms` is populated when is_sent=true; callers can set is_sent without a timestamp, or leave is_sent=false while status="sent".
findings.fix: Fold into the status enum (e.g. `LedgerStatus::Sent { sent_at: InstantOrEpochMs }`) so sent-state and timestamp are a single atomic type.

findings.problem: `pub id: String` is a primitive string with no domain constraints. Per the functional-core-performance reference, replace primitive domain APIs with newtypes when the value has domain rules.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid, empty, or malformed ledger IDs can flow through the core without any type-level enforcement or validation at the boundary.
findings.fix: Introduce a `LedgerId` newtype with a fallible constructor (e.g. `LedgerId::new(s: &str) -> Result<LedgerId, ParseError>`) and parse at boundaries into the trusted type.

findings.problem: `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` uses Option as a lifecycle field. Per the functional-core-performance reference, Option lifecycle fields must be replaced with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: The timestamp is semantically decoupled from the sent flag; the compiler cannot enforce that a sent ledger always has a timestamp.
findings.fix: Move the timestamp into the sent-state variant of the status enum so it only exists when the ledger is actually sent.

findings.problem: `mark_sent` blindly overwrites `status` and `is_sent` without checking prior state. Any caller can call it regardless of whether the ledger was already sent, validated, or in an invalid state.
findings.failure_mode: Idempotency violation: a ledger can be re-sent arbitrarily. No preconditions (e.g. must be validated first) are enforced at the type or function level.
findings.fix: Constrain the input type via a typestate wrapper (e.g. `MarkSentRequest { inner: ValidatedLedger }`) or return a `Result` from a fallible constructor so only validated ledgers can be marked sent.

findings.problem: `item.status = "sent".to_string()` allocates a new String from a literal. Combined with the fact that `status` is a String rather than an enum, this is unnecessary heap allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation in a hot path; the string literal should be an enum variant, eliminating heap allocation entirely.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with a `LedgerStatus` enum; set via `item.status = LedgerStatus::Sent` with zero allocation.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent performance
no profiler data for allocation patterns
no allocation audit (try_reserve, checked arithmetic, etc.)
no benchmark/profiler evidence for the stated performance characteristics
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The core issue is architectural — the type model allows illegal states by construction. No amount of runtime checks can fully close this gap; the fix requires type-level refactoring as described above.
